newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends a touch lower, chip stocks on fire.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends a touch lower, chip stocks on fire.

text.p: The Dow industrials ended a touch lower, snapping a four-day winning streak as bonds sold off on renewed rate jitters, but stocks were cushioned by a high-tech rally ignited by Intel's more bullish outlook.

"Stocks are doing great against bonds. If the Fed tightens, it will get very ugly in the stock market next week. We priced it out and would undo a lot of the advance of the past two weeks. But from the point of view of stocks, bonds have cried wolf alot," said David Shulman of Salomon Brothers. After back-to-back records, the Dow lost 0.37 to about 5889.

The blue chip index rallied 178.66 points last week to its second biggest weekly point gain ever, as some August economic reports pointed to moderating U.S. growth and tame inflation. The Dow on Monday rose 50.68 on continued buying momentum.

The tech-studded Nasdaq Composite surged nine points or 0.78 percent to about 1203, drawing nearer to June 5's all-time high finish of 1249.15. Technology stocks, especially semiconductor and semiconductor equipment makers, were bolstered by Intel's surprise announcement after Monday's market close that it expects third-quarter revenues to be even better than previously forecast.
Intel rocketed up 5-5/8 to 94-1/4 after hitting an intraday year-high of 95. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's semiconductor index jumped five percent to 181.87.

Texas Instruments rose 1-3/4 to 50-5/8, Applied Materials was up 1-5/8 to 27-3/8, Micron added 1-1/8 to 26-3/4 and Atmel surged 4-1/8 to 28-1/4. Losers outpaced gainers 14-9 on heavy NYSE volume of about 440 million shares.

The long bond tumbled 29/32, boosting its yield to 7.02 percent. Reuters quoted an unidentified senior Fed official as saying eight of the 12 district banks in the Federal Reserve System have requested a hike in the 5.0 percent discount rate.

The source said of the eight, three have requested a 50 basis point discount rate rise. The Fed consensus is seen around a 25 basis point federal funds rate rise on September 24, the source said. The Dow skidded nearly 40 points after the report before slashing losses.

"The bottom line is we were down nearly 40 and came back. When you get a run like this to new highs and this kind of momentum and pickup in volume, you rarely get an inverted 'V' straight up, straight down. Even if trouble is cooking out there, it would be a little selloff," said Ralph Bloch, chief technical analyst at Raymond James.

Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said: "Technology stocks are doing better and that's helping the general market...I'd be surprised to see a big market downer for awhile. We may back and fill for a few days, but the momentum seems very strong. Because of that, interest fears are somewhat mollified.
"I also think tobacco stocks helped market sentiment."

Tobacco stocks rose after news a judge dismissed pre-1994 claims in a Medicaid lawsuit brought against the industry by Florida. Florida Governor Lawton Chiles said the key points in the lawsuit remained intact.
Philip Morris added two to 94, RJR Nabisco Holdings, parent of R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, rose 1/2 to 27 and smokeless tobacco maker UST Inc rose 1-1/4 to 30-7/8.
Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon, said stocks were starting to adjust to a seven percent long bond yield.
"Stocks are looking ahead. If the economy is slowing and unemployment is rising, bonds can go to 6.5 percent quickly."

Among individual stocks, Compaq Computer rose 3-5/8 to 65. Prudential reiterated a strong buy after a bullish meeting with company executives on Monday. Solectron rose 5-3/8 to 47-3.8. Merrill upgraded the stock.

Loewen rose 6-1/4 to 40 in U.S. trading and Service Corp slipped 1/8 to 30-1/8 after Service offered to buy Loewen in a stock-for-stock exchange valuing Loewen at $43 a share. Loewen said it would review the offer. The bid comes as both funeral home operators have been buying North America's privately owned funeral homes.

United Cos Financial slumped 3-5/8 to 33-1/2. The company said some brokers cut earnings estimates after being disappointed by the expected size of the company's quarterly, asset backed debt securitization.
Interest rate sensitive stocks were weaker.
Freddie Mac lost 2-3/4 to 95, Fannie Mae was off 3/4 to 33-5/8, Citicorp lost 1-1/8 to 87-3/4 and Wells Fargo slipped 3-1/4 to 260-3/4.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 9.35 to 1203.31, its first close above 1200 since June 17's 1207.64.
The S&P 500 index fell 1.04 to 682.94.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk, 212 859 1721
